q: Is type as a list such as [string, null] valid OpenAPI, and whose problem is it when a tool rejects it?
a: It is valid OpenAPI 3.1, which adopts JSON Schema 2020-12 where type is one name or a list of them, and the list is how 3.1 states a nullable field. 3.0 allowed one name and spelled it nullable: true. Proven rather than asserted: redocly lint on the conformant spec reports only style rules and nothing structural, and a control run with the null entries changed to 99 produces one struct error per tampered entry with the message that type can be one of object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, null, addressed at type/1 of the array. So the validator does check inside the list and accepts it. nimo modelled Schema.Type as a scalar pointer with a 3.0 Nullable field beside it while its own generator emitted openapi 3.1.0, so it could not read what it wrote. Fixed in v1.0.24 with a SchemaType list that unmarshals either shape and marshals back the shape it got. nimo also enforces house rules beyond the standard in converter/main.go: servers, servers[0].url, an operationId on every operation and a summary or description on every path.
